note: The tools a part's processing can use (0.11): the skill's own mix fields and effects, Surge XT Effects' types and the Airwindows algorithms inside it, one entry each, read by studio.py effects (musiclib/effectscatalog.py). The words (kinds, summary, character, roles) are written in this project from the sources each entry names; an Airwindows algorithm's summary paraphrases its author's own descriptions. The controls, limits and defaults are references/surge-fx.json's. A fragment is a starting point to adapt: the table's defaults for a Surge XT effect, a setting of this project's own for the skill's tools, none taken from a preset. `measured` is each effect at its defaults after 4 s of silence (research/effects-0.11/surgefx_measure.py), on a decaying A minor chord peaking at -12 dBFS and the 6 s after it (level_db, the change of level; brightness_ratio, of the spectral centroid; width_db, side under mid from a mono input, floored at -60; tail_s, until the output falls 60 dB under the chord's level, at most 6 s), a 1 kHz sine at -12 dBFS (harmonics_db and inharmonic_db, the energy at the sine's harmonics and elsewhere against the sine's), and silence (noise_dbfs). `measured_words` follow from those by the rules in `word_rules`: they describe the defaults on those signals, not every setting. `repeat`: exact (the same samples each render), rounding (Tape: within -120 dBFS), or exact unless a `varies_when` rule holds, when the effect renders otherwise each time the part is processed anew (the cache keeps one take). `fallback`: a tool of the skill's own that does a related job where Surge XT Effects is not installed (the part itself then plays without its chain, and the render says so).

tools.summary: EQ bands: peaks, low and high shelves and notches, to cut what masks and lift what defines.
tools.watch: Cut before boosting where the move is narrow, and judge the part in the mix, not alone.

tools.summary: FFmpeg's compressor: ratio, attack, release, knee, make-up, parallel mix, peak or RMS detection.
tools.watch: Judge its shape, not its loudness: a fast attack softens the hits, a release too fast pumps. It acts after the part's level is set and is not undone: the louder notes come down, so the part comes out quieter unless makeup_db or a higher threshold makes up for it (schema.md).

tools.summary: A noise gate first among the part's processors: silences it below a threshold.
tools.watch: Set its threshold above the noise and under the quietest note meant to sound; a longer release keeps the tails of ringing notes.

tools.summary: Saturation at four times the rate with the level kept: tanh, atan, alg or erf curves.
tools.watch: Stacked saturation builds up the low mids: compare with the part without it at the same level.

tools.summary: A guitar amplifier and loudspeaker on the whole part, voices clean to high gain, and a bass voice.
tools.watch: Stacked saturation builds up the low mids: compare with the part without it at the same level. Made for a bank recorded from a pickup (fsbs_direct) or the three measured bass banks; on another, write input_db once the receipt's amp.input_peak is known.

tools.summary: Echoes on the beat, each landing on the tempo map to the sample, ping-pong and filters.
tools.watch: Filtering the repeats' highs darkens them and pushes them back.

tools.summary: The part pulled down on another part's notes, as a sidechain compressor keyed by the kick.
tools.watch: Judge its shape, not its loudness: a fast attack softens the hits, a release too fast pumps. It follows another part's notes: name that part in `by`. The part comes down by depth_db on each of them; its level_dbfs is its level between them.

tools.summary: A low- or high-pass filter moved along points in beats.
tools.watch: Wide modulation can lose level in mono: the analysis reports the mix's side against its mid.

tools.summary: A rhythmic gate by pattern on the beat grid.
tools.watch: Judge its shape, not its loudness: a fast attack softens the hits, a release too fast pumps. Its closed steps fall by depth_db; the part's level is set before it.

tools.summary: Tape speed variation: slow wow and fast flutter, no net drift in time.
tools.watch: Check that the part still speaks in the mix.

tools.summary: The skill's own chorus: two voices whose delays sweep, light and simple.
tools.watch: Wide modulation can lose level in mono: the analysis reports the mix's side against its mid.

tools.summary: FFmpeg's phaser.
tools.watch: Wide modulation can lose level in mono: the analysis reports the mix's side against its mid.

tools.summary: FFmpeg's bit and rate reducer, with a mix.
tools.watch: Check that the part still speaks in the mix.

tools.summary: FFmpeg's tremolo: level modulation.
tools.watch: Wide modulation can lose level in mono: the analysis reports the mix's side against its mid.

tools.summary: FFmpeg's flanger.
tools.watch: Wide modulation can lose level in mono: the analysis reports the mix's side against its mid.

tools.summary: A two-pole high-pass on the part (12 dB per octave), 30 Hz by default: clears what lies under the part's lowest notes.
tools.watch: Cut before boosting where the move is narrow, and judge the part in the mix, not alone.

tools.summary: A two-pole low-pass on the part, 18 kHz by default: takes the edge off a bright sample or sets a part back.
tools.watch: Cut before boosting where the move is narrow, and judge the part in the mix, not alone.

tools.summary: A send to the mix's reverb (on the bus chain, to its room, plate, hall or church): the space the parts share.
tools.watch: A long tail runs into the notes after it; the piece needs clock.tail_seconds for the last tail. Shared by the parts that send to it; the bus chain has four spaces, the room chain one.

tools.summary: A send to the mix's simple delay, delay_quarters long at the opening tempo.
tools.watch: Filtering the repeats' highs darkens them and pushes them back.

tools.summary: The part swung to and fro across the stereo image over a period of beats: an auto-pan (mix.move as a swing).
tools.watch: Wide modulation can lose level in mono: the analysis reports the mix's side against its mid. A moving part is folded to one channel first, so it takes no width or depth_m; in a loop it must stand at the loop's end where it stood at its start.

tools.summary: The 1980s gated reverb behind a drum machine's snares and claps: a dense room held, then cut.
